title: EFC (I) Ltd - 512008 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: EFC (I) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to ₹282.88 crore and PAT rose 52% YoY to ₹70.85 crore, with PAT margin at 25.1%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was ₹282.88 crore, up about 29% YoY, and EBITDA was ₹122.96 crore, up about 20% YoY at a 43.5% margin. PAT grew about 52% YoY to ₹70.85 crore, helped by lower finance cost, which management attributed to rationalised borrowing costs. Leasing remained the largest segment at ₹153.91 crore revenue, while Design & Build and Furniture grew strongly YoY but Design & Build fell sequentially from about ₹120 crore in Q4. Analysts pressed on sequential EBITDA decline (down about 14% QoQ), Furniture margin compression, and the planned demerger/restructuring.

financial_highlights.change: +29% YoY (from ₹219.62 crore); down about 3% QoQ per analyst
+20% YoY (from ₹102.16 crore); down about 14% QoQ per analyst

segments.name: Leasing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹153.91 crore (+26% YoY from ₹122.18 crore); segment result ₹64.33 crore. Managed workspace across 25 cities with over 84,000 total seats and over 68,000 billed seats.

segments.name: Design & Build
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹100.39 crore (vs ₹84.69 crore in Q1 FY26, about +19% YoY); segment result ₹33.84 crore. Order book above ₹228 crore, with management saying over 85% is external third-party work.

segments.name: Furniture (Ek Design)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹28.57 crore (+124% YoY from ₹12.75 crore); segment result only ₹2.10 crore, a thin margin of about 7%. Order book about ₹53 crore; over 2,200 SKUs and over 75,000 units delivered to date.

guidance_outlook: Management is 100% confident of adding 18,000-20,000 billable seats in Leasing this fiscal year.
Design & Build targeted at roughly 50% YoY growth for FY27, which management says is backed by the existing order book.
Furniture expected to deliver similar growth; management expects EBITDA above 25% in the vertical at optimal capacity utilisation (60-70%), targeted by end of this year.
Margins are described as stable to improving, with no specific consolidated margin guidance given.
Demerger/restructuring: all subsidiaries to consolidate under EFC (I) Ltd, with EFC Ltd merged in and an asset-holding company kept as a wholly owned subsidiary; no timeline given on the call.
capex_capacity: Managed workspace capacity: over 84,000 total seats and over 68,000 billed seats across 25 cities; more inventory under development without revenue commitment.
Asset monetisation model: acquires vacant assets (about 10 years old), refurbishes and leases them via managed office, capturing rental yield and grade-upgrade appreciation.
Fit-out payback is about 18-20 months per seat on a ₹50,000 per-seat cost, which management says is standard across cities and funded mainly by landlords.
Furniture plant is still scaling; management says optimal utilisation is 60-70% and expects to approach it by end of FY27.
Borrowings are mainly LAP and LRD facilities tied to acquired assets; management says borrowing costs have been rationalised.
demand_pricing: Average occupancy stated at 90%+ and enterprise retention at about 95%+ (churn 4-5%); average enterprise client tenure rose to 51 months.
Enterprise demand from GCCs, MNCs, BFSI, technology, consulting and outsourcing firms.

D&B order book rose to over ₹228 crore from ₹135 crore at end of Q4 FY26, with over ₹100 crore of Q4 orders already executed. Management says Q1 is seasonally slow and projects typically ramp in Q3-Q4.
Competition named on the call: Awfi, Smartworks, WeWork India, IndiQube and large landlords; management cites price, speed of execution, design and fit-out cost optimisation as differentiators.
Management says supply-chain and material-price disruptions persist but have not stopped YoY growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the D&B (₹228 crore) and Furniture (₹53 crore) order books is third-party versus internal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 85% is from external clients, since most internal fit-out work is already done by landlords.

qa_highlights.question: Why did D&B revenue fall from about ₹120 crore in Q4 to about ₹100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said D&B is project-based with no seasonality; Q1 is typically slow, and projects ramp in Q3-Q4. It reiterated a roughly 50% YoY growth target.

qa_highlights.question: Furniture revenue rose 36% QoQ but segment margin fell from about 75% to about 7%; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing was wrong and that the business is still below optimal utilisation. It expects a stabilised EBITDA above 25% at 60-70% utilisation, and said QoQ margin comparison is not meaningful yet.

qa_highlights.question: Occupancy, retention and seat addition guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy is 90%+, retention about 95%+, and 18,000-20,000 billable seat additions are targeted with full confidence.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT rise while revenue and EBITDA fell QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the EBITDA dip to Ind AS accounting effects and pointed to PAT as the better measure. It cited lower borrowing costs, cost control, and Leasing performance.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates EFC against Awfi, Smartworks, WeWork India and IndiQube, and what is the city mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the integrated real-estate-as-a-service model, three revenue streams, economies of scale, design and fit-out cost optimisation. It said the West is strongest; North and South are each above 15%; focus cities are 10 (3 North, 3 South, 3 West, plus Kolkata).

risks_watch: Sequential decline: revenue down about 3% and EBITDA down about 14% QoQ, with Design & Build lower than Q4; D&B growth depends on Q3-Q4 project ramp-up.
Furniture segment margin of about 7% in Q1 versus 25%+ target; sustainability depends on reaching 60-70% utilisation.
Reported PAT growth is driven partly by lower finance costs; watch interest cost and LAP/LRD leverage as asset-monetisation capex grows.
Demerger/restructuring details (timeline, tax treatment, accounting impact) were not specified and need follow-up.
Competitive intensity from Awfi, Smartworks, WeWork India, IndiQube and landlords; supply-chain and material-price pressures on D&B.
key_quotes: There's nothing wrong in the Furniture segment.
The EBITDA reduction is primarily because of the way the Ind AS accounting works.
100% confident on kind of adding about 18,000 to 20,000 billable seats on the Leasing business.
There's no seasonality, which is kind of affecting this business.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order book visibility and the 50% D&B and 18,000-20,000 seat targets, but defensive on the sequential decline, Furniture margin (about 7%) and the EBITDA dip, which management attributed to Ind AS effects and pointed to PAT instead. Restructuring answers were high-level, with no timeline or accounting detail given.
